title: Length of Longest Subarray With at Most K Frequency
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the length of the longest subarray where each element's frequency does not exceed k.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the length of the longest subarray where each element's frequency does not exceed k. A subarray is a consecutive segment of the array.
constraints: nums is nonempty and k is a positive integer no larger than nums length.
A subarray is good when no value occurs more than k times.
Return the maximum length of a contiguous good subarray.
hints: After adding the right value, only that value can newly violate the frequency cap.
Maintain counts in a sliding window and advance left until the new value is within its limit.
Increment nums[right]; while its count exceeds k, decrement nums[left] and move left; maximize width.
The left boundary stops at the earliest valid start for each right endpoint, so that window is the longest valid one ending there.
editorial: The left boundary stops at the earliest valid start for each right endpoint, so that window is the longest valid one ending there.

tests.explanation: The first six values contain each number exactly twice, and every longer window overuses one or two.
Any four consecutive values are valid, while a fifth copy exceeds the limit.
